note: Hand-curated calibration, kept OUT of proto_catalog.json because that file is regenerated from proto-tools on every `litkb proto-sync` and everything in it is derived. Keyed by (tool, metric): one model emits several metrics and may be characterised for some and not others. Overlaid at build time by proto.apply_calibration. Tool-level `status` is DERIVED from these, never curated.
promotion_rule: A metric becomes "validated" only on measured reliability against a held-out benchmark, per docs/PRD-framework.md section 6, and the record must carry `measured_error` and `benchmark` or it is refused. Absence means needs_calibration; silence is never a promotion.
known_gaps: Exactly one metric is calibrated: esmfold-prediction:avg_plddt, at a resolution of 0.0596 pLDDT measured on 34 in-band chains of a 100-chain held-out benchmark. Every other (tool, metric) pair in the catalogue remains needs_calibration, so section 6 still forbids ranking on all of them. `applicability_domain` is recorded and still not enforced against anything: there is no candidate set yet to check it against.

The promoted fit rests on 34 chains, not the 60-100 the benchmark was sized for: only 34 of the 100 measured chains cleared the avg_plddt >= 0.7 slope band (measured span 0.365-0.903). It clears MIN_ROWS and the 2x-standard-error test, but it is thinner than intended and a wider high-confidence set would tighten it.
Only 48 of 140 catalogued tools emit metrics at all; the other 92 are generators, retrievers, aligners and annotators for which calibration is meaningless. The real calibration surface is those 48.

Nothing distinguishes a curator from anyone with write access to this file. `apply_calibration` checks that a `validated` record is well-formed -- a positive numeric `measured_error.value` and a `benchmark` -- but enforces no authority check on who supplies it. Framework section 11 Q5 leaves 'who may promote' open, and this promotion changed what the whole system is permitted to claim.

benchmark.name: PDB post-cutoff single chains
benchmark.cutoff_source: Lin et al., bioRxiv 2022.07.20.500902, 'Structure training sets for ESMFold'
benchmark.selection: RCSB search: exptl.method=X-RAY DIFFRACTION, deposited chains 1-3, entity length 40-500. NO date constraint -- the cutoff is applied by benchmark.select so the filter the held-out claim rests on is exercised on real entries rather than pre-satisfied by the query.
limitations: Every post-cutoff entry in the sampled pool fell in a single 2026 window; RCSB's default result ordering returned a bimodal sample (1976-1999 and 2026, nothing between). The set is therefore ~6 years past the training cutoff -- conservative for leakage -- but spans only about six months of depositions, so it is narrower in time than a benchmark drawn across 2020-2026 would be.

No homology screen was run against pre-cutoff structures. A post-cutoff entry can be a point mutant or close homolog of a structure ESMFold trained on, so the date filter bounds memorisation of that exact entry, not generalisation.

n_chains is deposited_polymer_entity_instance_count, pinned against a live RCSB response (1UBQ reports 1). This is the deposited chain count, which is what the runner's single-protein-chain guard checks.

applicability_domain.notes: single chains only; measured on this benchmark set
